purpose: Replace mistaken dolphin identity with existing gray shark; rebuild original mouth anatomy.

arguments.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Redraw Image 1, the exact original SLEVEJM2 011 sprite, as one polished cartoon SHARK sprite. Image 1 controls pose, mouth shape, facing, visible anatomy, framing and water occlusion. Images 2 and 3 are CHARACTER DESIGN AND DRAWING STYLE ONLY, not pose. Match the established shark: neutral medium gray skin, pale ivory jaw and underside, gill slits, bold black outlines, smooth restrained cel shading, heavy sly brows and razor-sharp triangular teeth. This is the sneaky shark character, never a friendly dolphin; no dolphin beak or rounded dolphin teeth. Pose: Shark leans back and looks toward upper-right with open mischievous mouth, sharp triangular upper and lower teeth and red-pink mouth interior. Both eyes high on head, brows sly. Broad pale ivory belly faces viewer. Pectoral fin on image-left raises high along side of head with its tip up; other fin reaches nearly horizontally to image-right. Preserve the two fin directions and backward lean, not a neutral symmetric pose. Lower body absent below the original waterline. Preserve the source silhouette and relative positions while replacing pixel steps with smooth ink. Only the character parts above water are drawn, with a thin cyan-and-white ripple at original cutoff. Do not complete submerged body, tail or legs. One character only. All contours inside canvas with clear transparent padding on every edge. Actual transparent RGBA background, no checkerboard, scene, cast shadow, glow, text or collage.
